stage: blind-parallel A — may two browser suites run at once on this host, and under which conditions
verbatim: docs/1455-step1-eval-a.md (the ids below are the merger's normalisation of that text: V = verdict, R/C/T = the author's own ids, U = the tooling bullets in order, T0 = the test's common protocol)

entries.defect: VERDICT: YES-UNDER-CONDITIONS, not yet allowed; the 1452 data cannot decide it. Bottleneck is one heavy-job slot (33.3 h acceptance vs 7.1 h authoring; 15.8 h finished suites + ~4.3 h hung). M3 pair 13m 44s/13m 39s vs 18m 56.5s serial = 27 % gain on an unbalanced pair, ~45 % balanced; per-suite slowdown 1.5–3.5 %. The 1452 rule judged single-suite duration, the wrong measure. Pairing pays while the induced red rate stays under ~10–20 % (a false red costs 20–30 min vs 5–12 min saved). Real gain smaller: pairs exist only for two backends of one point or two points in acceptance; fix loops (73 % of suite minutes) do not pair; estimate 15–30 % less suite wall clock (2–5 h per 70 h), calibratable. Why not yet: 4 overlapped runs bound the added red rate only below 53 %; M3 ran in one checkout with contaminated frame verdicts; no WebGL 2, no timing probe, no full suite.

R1 Shared frame directory → false approval. framesWrittenSince counts distinct names by mtime in <checkout>/verification/ with no run identity; a run short of frames is masked by the partner's frames; the hang sampler (run-logged.mjs) is kept alive by the partner's frames so a wedged run's HUNG verdict is delayed. Certain in one checkout (measured: water-stand-table 2 quiet vs 13/14 overlapped; villager-dress 28 vs 30). None across checkouts because OUT and FRAME_DIR resolve per checkout root.

R2 The second-started run is labelled loaded: machine-load counts the partner as a verifyRun stray, every polish suite is timing-sensitive, so action is flag and the log says its timing verdicts do NOT count as evidence. Conflicts with a-red-stays-a-red: a real red could be waved off as load. The first-started run carries no label (asymmetric). Certain for the second-started run.

R3 Memory. Idle ~17 %; solo peaks villager-dress 66 % (+49 points), water-stand-table 38–40 % (+23). The pair reached 73–75 % only because the peaks did not coincide (17+49+23 = 89 % > 85 %). Two heavy sections: 17+49+49 ≈ 115 % = swap or OOM under WSL2. Full polish-villagers (43 min) and LARGE never memory-sampled; villager-dress peaks in its last minute. High for heavy+heavy, low for heavy+light.

R4 GPU contention cannot be seen: both lanes reach the same GPU through /dev/dxg (WebGPU, and WebGL 2 via Mesa d3d12); machine-load reports GPU load NOT measured. Medium; shows only indirectly as lower frame rate → R5 reds and longer durations.

R5 Timing-sensitive checks: at a lower frame rate settle and shutter windows slip; the rotating WebGL 2 adult-errands checks are exactly this kind. Firing counts in 15 WebGL 2 runs since 18.10: jar mouth under water 3, foam drifted after shutter 3, filmed adult walks on between frames 2, order-at-stand 6; WebGPU sprint 5 in 26. water-stand-table WebGL 2 'one whole water errand recorded … frames, timeout' is red on every recent WebGL 2 run (frame-budget bound). Medium–high; shows as a higher firing rate of these names in overlapped runs.
R6 WebGL 2 is more load-sensitive than WebGPU (villager-dress WebGL 2 6/9 green vs WebGPU 25/26); M3 had no WebGL 2 at all. Medium, unmeasured; a WebGL 2 red that appears only in pairs.

R7 LARGE runs: 115–121 min both-backend with build and preview, the closing and bundle evidence; memory profile unknown; a pair stretches the window in which contention can hit. High cost if wrong; a LARGE red that does not reproduce.

R8 Picture checks and screenshot timing: frames under contention can catch a late glTF body arrival, LOD or settle state; shutter checks catch a missing subject but not every quality difference; picture-stability metrics would drift if calibrated from pair runs. Low–medium.

R9 Ports: _server.mjs takes an OS-assigned port (listen 0), closes it, binds vite with --strictPort, one retry; gpu-backend-probe and ttsCache use listen(0); Playwright uses a pipe and a temporary profile. Negligible.

R10 Shared state across checkouts: .claude/render-verify-state.json is an unlocked read-modify-write (atomic rename, last writer wins) so two exits at once can lose one run record — fails closed (a rerun, not a false green). Worktree node_modules is a symlink to the main one, so node_modules/.vite/deps is shared: a checkout with a different lockfile or vite config re-optimizes under the partner's server (reload or 504). run-wait.mjs with no log refuses when two runs are live (U13): safe. Low.
R11 Same-section same-backend pair in one checkout: identical frame names overwrite each other, so a picture judgement would read the other run's frame. Certain if done; forbidden by C2.
R12 A third load beside a pair: M1 accepted only one remote review beside one suite; unit, build or lint beside a suite is rejected (M2, +12 %). Forbidden by C6.

C1 Admission by pairing, not globally: pair two suites/sections only if both have a measured solo memory profile and either the coincident-peak sum (idle + Δa + Δb) ≤ 85 % or T1 measured the pair peak ≤ 80 % over ≥ 5 pairs. heavy+heavy (two villager-dress-class runs) stays forbidden until T1 shows otherwise.

C2 Separate checkouts: each pair member runs in its own checkout so verification/, dist/ and the frame counter are separate (fixes R1, R11). For one point's two backends the second runs from a worktree at the same SHA. Check that the both-backend guard credits a run recorded from that worktree (branch/head keying in render-verify-state); if not, use the point's own worktree plus the main tree on the same SHA.
C3 Same deps: both checkouts identical in package.json, package-lock.json and vite.config.* (R10). A branch that changes dependencies runs solo.
C4 Own port per run — already true (_server.mjs). Change nothing; never pin --port.
C5 Never in a pair: LARGE and closing runs; benchmark, voice, touch and startup; picture-stability calibration runs; full polish suites until their solo memory profile is measured.
C6 Nothing else heavy beside a pair: no unit, build or lint gate and no local agent (M2). A remote review stays allowed only beside a single suite (M1 is not proven for pairs).
C7 Memory sampled: sample every 5 s for every pair and abort the later-started member if a sample is > 85 %, using the existing /proc/meminfo sampling from 1452, not a new guard.

C8 A red stays a red: the R2 loaded label is informational only. A red in either member is charged like a quiet red, never filed to the charge ledger as load, never covered by a retry (a retry is SUSPECT).

C9 Stop rule: any uncharged red in an overlapped run, a memory sample > 85 % or a HUNG run switches pair mode off (bound back to 1). Pair mode returns only after a quiet rerun of the red section on the same build: reproduces quiet → belongs to its owning point, pair mode resumes; does not reproduce in 2 quiet runs → overlap-attributed, pair mode stays off until that cause is diagnosed and filed.
C10 Waits name their log: always call run-wait.mjs <log> with the log path, never the newest-live default.

T0 Common protocol: one build (the 1452 same-build git diff --quiet set), quiet host, no other heavy job; every run through run-logged.mjs; memory sampled every 5 s with a shared pair log; every pair in two separate checkouts (C2); the later member starts 60 s after the first so the heavy phases overlap.

T1 Solo memory profiles (quiet references): one sampled solo run each of villager-dress WebGPU and WebGL 2, water-stand-table WebGPU, water-jar-carried WebGL 2 and adult-errands WebGL 2 → Δpeak above idle for C1. Existing data reused: villager-dress WebGPU 66 %, water-stand-table 38–40 %.

T2 Quiet duration and red references on the test build: villager-dress WebGPU 5 (3 exist on 9044a6684 if same-build), water-stand-table WebGPU 3, water-jar-carried WebGL 2 3, villager-dress WebGL 2 3, adult-errands WebGL 2 10 (base firing rate of each rotating check name).

T3 Known-green detector pairs (zero-red test) with sections of clean record: villager-dress WebGPU (25/26) and water-jar-carried WebGL 2 (5/5); water-stand-table WebGPU accepted from M3. Block A (WebGPU+WebGPU): villager-dress ‖ water-stand-table, 3 new pairs (M3's 2 void for frames). Block B (mixed backend, the real both-backend case): villager-dress WebGPU ‖ water-jar-carried WebGL 2, 5 pairs. Block D (WebGL 2 + WebGL 2): water-jar-carried ‖ adult-errands, 5 pairs, only if T1 admits (C1). Pass: 0 overlap-attributed reds (C9 attribution) in ≥ 30 known-green member runs (bounds the added red rate below 9.5 % at 95 %); at most 1 attributed red only if 15 more pairs then show 0 (≥ 60 runs, bound ≈ 5 %); ≥ 2 attributed reds FAIL. With a base red rate ~4 % plain 0-reds over 30 runs fails by chance ~70 %, hence attribution through a quiet rerun first.

T4 Timing-sensitive probe (WebGL 2) on adult-errands: 5 villager-dress WebGPU runs (13 min) as partners, each hosting 2 back-to-back adult-errands WebGL 2 runs (~5 min) → 10 overlapped runs; partners count toward T3. Counted per run: firing of each rotating check name (jar mouth, foam drift, filmed adult walks on, order-at-stand, sprint, heading-in-one-frame); the steady charged rim/handover pair excluded. FAIL if total rotating firings overlapped > quiet + max(3, 50 % of quiet); or a name fires ≥ 2× overlapped that never fired in the 10 quiet runs; or one-sided Fisher on any-rotating-red per run gives p < 0.10. Limit: n = 10 per arm at base 20–40 % detects only ~2× rise; a smaller effect is left to the C9 stop rule in live use.

T5 Throughput, read off T3/T4: pair wall clock ≤ 0.80 × the sum of the quiet medians (median over pairs); each member ≤ 1.15 × its quiet median so run-wait's runtime and ceiling expectations stay valid; the 1452 above-the-quiet-median rule recorded, not used to judge. After admission, landed points per hour over the next real cycle compared with the post-1444 control (2.53 h per point); pair mode stays only if not worse.
T6 Memory: no sample > 85 % in any pair; a pair admitted under the C1 measured-peak branch needs every peak ≤ 80 %.

T7 Frame integrity: in every pair each member's framesWritten equals its solo T2 count (e.g. water-stand-table 2, not 13); proves C2 works; any cross-count FAIL. Order: T1, T2, T4 (riskiest), T3 B, T3 D, T3 A; stop at first FAIL. Host time ≈ 2.75 h quiet references + ≈ 3.75 h pairs ≈ 6.5 h unattended; early FAIL stops after ~2 h.
U1 Runbook Local heavy jobs: change bound 1 to 2 browser suites under C1–C10, only after T1–T7 pass; replace the M3 REJECTED line with the T-result; keep POOL_CAP untouched.
U2 1452 step 5 doc: note the M3 frame counts are cross-contaminated (R1) and that its decision rule measured duration, not throughput.

U3 Load label (R2): pair runs use the existing --on-load=flag; the runbook states the label never discounts a red (C8); alternatively --on-load=off, which still reports the load; never defer (the second member would skip).
U4 Frame directory (R1): separate checkouts (C2) instead of a new run-identity field. HOA_FRAME_DIR is no fix because suites write to OUT, resolved per checkout.
U5 run-wait.mjs: change nothing; always pass the log (C10).
U6 Memory sampling: reuse the 1452 /proc/meminfo 5 s sampling; a sample over 85 % is the abort signal (C7).
U7 README: add one paragraph — pairs only across checkouts, never for LARGE, benchmark, voice or touch.

U8 Open item: check whether the both-backend guard credits a run recorded from a same-SHA second worktree (C2). If not, that is a current blockade of pair use, fixable under the freeze rule; note it in docs/backlog.md.
